parsed.headline: Student killed in Riyadh airport attack

pages.text: A student was killed during an attack on a passenger terminal at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Lamis Asiri, a final-year student at Prince Musaid bin Abdulrahman University in Abha, was waiting in the departure area for a flight back to Abha with her mother following a medical appointment when the attack occurred. Asiri's mother survived the incident and is recovering from her injuries. The General Authority of Civil Aviation initially reported that 12 people were killed and 309 were injured, including several individuals in critical condition. Asiri's father told Al Arabiya that he is in shock and struggling to come to terms with the loss after his last communication with his daughter was a wish for a safe journey home.

parsed.headline: Hamburg court sentences two men to prison for plotting attacks on Jewish leaders for Iran

pages.text: A court in Hamburg, Germany, sentenced two men to multiple years in prison on Thursday for plotting to target Jewish leaders on behalf of Iran's secret service. According to DW World, both defendants were found guilty of espionage and attempted murder. One defendant, identified as a 54-year-old Dane with Afghan roots, received a four-and-a-half year sentence. The second defendant, a 43-year-old Afghan man living in Denmark, was sentenced to eight-and-a-half years for acting as the mastermind of the planned attacks. Prosecutors stated the 54-year-old had received orders directly from Iran's al-Quds Brigades, the foreign arm of the Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps. He reportedly recruited the 43-year-old to carry out an attack or find someone who could, and tasked him with finding a weapon. The court found the pair planned to attack Josef Schuster, the president of the Central Council of Jews in Germany, and Volker Beck, a Green Party politician and president of the German-Israeli society. Additionally, the 54-year-old had reportedly made preparations for an arson attack on a kosher deli in Berlin. The two men were arrested by Danish authorities in Aarhus last year before being extradited to Germany.

parsed.headline: 222,550 voters participate in advance voting for Toronto municipal election

pages.text: A total of 222,550 eligible voters participated during six days of advance voting for Toronto’s 2026 municipal election, which concluded on October 11, 2026, at 7 p.m., according to the City of Toronto. Election day is scheduled for October 12, 2026. On that day, eligible voters are required to vote at their assigned voting place as indicated on their Voter Information Card or the Toronto Elections webpage. Voters who requested to vote by mail must return their completed packages to Toronto Elections by October 7, 2026. To meet this deadline, the city advises using one of 25 secure, indoor yellow Mail-in Voting drop boxes located in each ward. These boxes are monitored by CCTV and emptied daily by election staff. Voters can use a confirmation code to verify if their mail-in ballot was received on time.

Registration for third party advertisers in the Toronto municipal election closes at 4:30 p.m. on October 9, 2026. Any person, corporation, or trade union intending to spend money to promote, support, or oppose a candidate must register as a third party advertiser. A Notice of Registration must be filed in person at the Toronto Elections City Hall office located at 100 Queen St. W., first floor, Permit Alley. Registrations can be filed between October 9, 2026, and October 12, 2026, from 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.

parsed.headline: Interfaith women urged to champion climate action in Ghana

pages.text: Women from Christian, Muslim, and traditional religious communities have been urged to take an active role in addressing climate change and protecting the environment. The call was made at the Faith to Action Women’s Conference held in Accra, Ghana, organized by the Centre for Interfaith Studies and Engagement in Africa (CISEA) under the theme “Women, Climate Justice and Sustainable Peace.” Participants discussed combining faith, climate action, and sustainable livelihoods to build peaceful communities.  Patricia Addy, the Director of the Presbyterian Women’s Centre, addressed the gathering, stating that climate change is no longer an abstract issue in Ghana due to experienced effects such as flooding, drought, water challenges, and changing weather patterns. Addy cited a situation in Abokobi, where residents recently relied on the women’s centre for water during a prolonged dry spell, as evidence of the need to protect natural resources. She noted that discussions on climate justice must include the impact of illegal mining, known as galamsey, on forests, water bodies, livelihoods, and future generations. Addy emphasized that women—serving as educators, farmers, mothers, entrepreneurs, and faith or community leaders—are particularly important to environmental protection and sustainable development efforts.  The conference guest speaker, Rev. Ebenezer Yaw Blasu, a lecturer at the Akrofi-Christaller Institute of Theology, Mission and Culture, stated that women are well positioned to champion environmental protection because of their role in sustaining and nurturing life. Blasu suggested that women could also create sustainable livelihoods by producing useful items from waste materials during environmental restoration efforts.

parsed.headline: Supreme Court of Canada to hear challenge to Ontario Place redevelopment legislation

pages.text: The Supreme Court of Canada plans to hear arguments on Thursday from a coalition challenging the constitutionality of legislation intended to facilitate major changes at Ontario Place in Toronto. The coalition, known as the Ontario Place Protectors, is contesting the Rebuilding Ontario Place Act (ROPA), alleging the law violates the Constitution by insulating state action from court scrutiny. The group also argues that exemptions from municipal noise regulations and environmental and heritage laws constitute a breach of public trust. The provincial government's redevelopment plan for the waterfront park includes a relocated Ontario Science Centre, a private company-operated spa, a provincial police detachment, a parking facility, and revamped shoreline and play areas. In January, the Supreme Court agreed to hear the case following unsuccessful legal challenges in lower courts. An Ontario judge dismissed the application in 2024, and a subsequent challenge in the provincial Court of Appeal was also unsuccessful. Writing for a unanimous Court of Appeal, Justice Grant Huscroft stated that while the government's decision is strongly opposed by various organizations and citizens, the court is not an alternative forum for resolving political grievances and found no basis to dismiss the provisions of ROPA on constitutional grounds.

parsed.headline: NDC launches six publications documenting party history in Ghana

pages.text: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) launched six publications in Accra, Ghana, on October 13, 2026, to document the party’s history, constitutional development, electoral manifestos, and contributions to the country's democratic governance. According to the Ghana News Agency, the initiative aims to preserve the party’s institutional memory and provide researchers and future generations with materials regarding its political journey and role in the Fourth Republic. One publication traces the NDC’s constitutional arrangements from 1992 to 2026, while another compiles election manifestos from 1992 to 2024. The remaining four volumes cover significant political developments, milestones in the Fourth Republic, and periods of political mobilisation in Ghana. Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang launched the books, stating they would support research and political education by providing insights into policy evolution, internal debates, and decisions. She encouraged regional and constituency executives, libraries, and research institutions to preserve copies for future reference. During the event, Professor Opoku-Agyemang purchased the first set of six publications for GH¢300,000. NDC Chairman Johnson Asiedu Nketia and the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod), Sammy Gyamfi, each purchased subsequent sets for GH¢300,000.

parsed.headline: Syria to rejoin Arab constituency at the IMF

pages.text: Syria will rejoin the Arab constituency at the International Monetary Fund (IMF) effective November 1, according to the Syrian Finance Ministry. This move ends Syria's membership in the Russian Federation’s group, which the country joined in 2012. The Syrian Arab News Agency reported that the announcement followed a meeting in Bangkok, Thailand, on the sidelines of the 2026 IMF and World Bank annual meetings. The meeting included Syrian Finance Minister Mohammed Yisr Barnieh, Central Bank Governor Mohammad Safwat Raslan, and Ali Al-Hosani, the executive director for the Arab constituency at the IMF. Officials discussed ongoing cooperation, such as technical assistance, capacity building, and preparations for Article IV consultations, which are regular assessments of member countries' economic policies. The IMF's last Article IV consultation with Syria took place in 2009. In August, the IMF stated that double-digit economic expansion was expected in 2026, with strong growth continuing into 2027, though data gaps remain a constraint on economic assessment.

parsed.headline: Trump administration officials suggest Fort Hood shooter's execution may not be live streamed following bipartisan backlash

pages.text: Following bipartisan criticism, Vice President JD Vance appeared to quell concerns on October 9, 2026, that the firing squad execution of Nidal Hasan would be live streamed. When asked by reporters how he squares his Christian faith with the Pentagon's decision to broadcast the execution, Vance stated, “First of all, I’ve seen these announcements. I don’t know that that’s actually going to happen.” This follows a statement made last week by Pete Hegseth to the broadcaster Real America’s Voice, in which he said the execution of Hasan would be available to watch online. Hasan’s sentence represents the first military execution in more than 60 years and would have been the first in U.S. history to be publicly broadcast. Democrats and several Republicans expressed concerns that live streaming the execution would align the United States with authoritarian countries that make a public “spectacle” of executions and could risk radicalizing viewers by turning Hasan into a martyr.
